gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Panasonic SC-PM270 has no AM band at all (Panasonic's North American spec lists only FM, 87.5–108 MHz, and AC 120 V only), or that on CD boomboxes AM comes only through a ferrite bar antenna inside the case, so you aim AM by turning the whole unit and the telescopic antenna is for FM only.
standout_why: Compared against bestspeakerreviews.com (Best CD AM FM Stereo Systems), dailydealhere.com (9 Best CD Boomboxes) and the Target CD-560 listing. bestspeakerreviews puts the Panasonic SC-PM270PP-K in an 'AM FM' roundup and flags only the MEGATEK as lacking AM. It never says the SC-PM270 is FM-only or explains AM antennas. dailydealhere already says the GPX's internal AM antenna responds to moving the boombox, names the MEGATEK as FM-only and covers CD-R finalization. So the general mechanism is partly covered (it doesn't reach 3). The new part is that Panasonic's own spec shows the SC-PM270 has no AM tuner, plus the makers' wording that the telescopic antenna is for FM and AM is aimed by turning the unit. That wording explains the Target reviewers' 'no antenna so signals are also weak' and 'Doesn't pick many AM stations' complaints about the Jensen CD-560. The Philips TAZ6000/10 that ChatGPT got is a DAB+/FM unit (EU suffix /10) with no AM band.
decides: For a US shopper who means AM/FM, this rules out FM-only units such as the Panasonic SC-PM270 (which Dealectric already lists), the Philips CD Soundmachine models ChatGPT showed as 'FM radio' and the DAB+/FM Philips TAZ6000/10. It points to AM/FM boomboxes with a built-in ferrite bar antenna: the Sony CFD-S70 (AM 530–1,710 kHz, ferrite bar), the Jensen CD-490 and CD-560, and the GPX BC112B. The page should tell buyers to turn the whole unit for AM, because pulling out the telescopic antenna only helps FM. If the shopper only wants FM, the SC-PM270 is still fine, but it has no battery power.

findings.label: Tuner bands
findings.value: FM only, 87.9–107.9 MHz (200 kHz step) / 87.5–108 MHz (100 kHz step), 30 presets; no AM band listed
findings.source_title: Feature and Specification - Audio - Compact stereo - Model SC-PM270K - Video (Panasonic North America support)
findings.note: Panasonic's own North American spec page. The tuner entry lists only FM ranges. Antenna terminal 75 ohm.

findings.label: Power source
findings.value: AC 120 V, 60 Hz mains only; no battery operation for the main unit
findings.source_title: Feature and Specification - Audio - Compact stereo - Model SC-PM270K - Video (Panasonic North America support)
findings.note: Dry batteries are listed only for the remote. Disc format CD-DA / MP3, with CD-R/RW supported.

findings.label: AM antenna mechanism
findings.value: AM uses a built-in ferrite bar antenna; Sony says to 'Reorient the unit itself for optimum reception'
findings.source_title: SONY CFD-S70 - Personal Audio System Manual and Review Video | ManualsLib
findings.note: Sony manual text as reproduced on ManualsLib. The specs list 'AM: Built-in ferrite bar antenna'. Troubleshooting also names mobile phones and other equipment that emits radio waves near the unit as noise sources, and says a small radio hum is 'not a malfunction'.

findings.label: Tuner ranges
findings.value: FM 87.5–108 MHz (100 kHz steps); AM 530–1,710 kHz (10 kHz steps)
findings.source_title: SONY CFD-S70 - Personal Audio System Manual and Review Video | ManualsLib
findings.note: Specifications section of the Sony manual.

findings.source_title: SONY CFD-S70 - Personal Audio System Manual and Review Video | ManualsLib

findings.value: 6 × R14 (C) batteries; about 10 h CD playback, about 15 h tape playback, about 23 h recording FM

findings.label: AM vs FM antenna

findings.note: The 'Holds vertically and reposition' line is paraphrased from the manual. This manual page gives power as AC 120 V, 60 Hz or 8 × C (UM-2) batteries. Retailers list 6 × C, so the manual may cover a different revision of the CD-490.
